question.text: In which year did the CBOT introduce the first exchange-traded derivative contracts (futures) in the US?

explanation.text: The Logic: While CBOT was established in 1848 for forward trading, the NISM Series VIII workbook records that in 1865 CBOT listed the first exchange-traded derivative contract in the US — standardised futures contracts that could be traded on the exchange. The Trap: 1848 is when CBOT was established (initially for forward contracts). 1919 is when CME was formed. 1972 is when the IMM (part of CME) launched currency futures. Note: The qualifier "in the US" matters — the workbook is specifically describing the first exchange-traded derivative contract in the United States, not globally.
